assume_role.description: Issue temporary credentials for an IAM role whose trust policy trusts the connected user or account. The result contains a secret access key and session token: anyone who can see this workflow's run history can use them until they expire.
assume_role.name: assume_role

parameters.description: The role to assume: its ARN (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/MyRole), or just the role's name for a role in the connected account.
parameters.name: role_arn

parameters.description: A name for this session, 2-64 letters, digits or _ + = , . @ -. It appears in the session's ARN and in CloudTrail.
parameters.name: role_session_name

parameters.description: How long the result stays valid, 900-43200 seconds. Default 3600; cannot exceed the role's maximum session duration.
parameters.name: duration_seconds

parameters.description: Optional IAM policy document (JSON) that further limits the session's permissions. It can only narrow them, never add any.
parameters.name: policy

parameters.description: Up to 10 managed policy ARNs (or AWS managed policy names such as 'ReadOnlyAccess') that further limit the session's permissions.
parameters.name: policy_arns

parameters.description: Optional tags passed into the session as key/value pairs.
parameters.name: tags

parameters.description: Session tag keys that carry over if this session assumes another role.
parameters.name: transitive_tag_keys

parameters.description: Only if the role's trust policy requires one (sts:ExternalId condition).
parameters.name: external_id

parameters.description: Only if MFA is required: the device's ARN (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:mfa/device-name), from IAM > Users > your user > Security credentials.
parameters.name: mfa_serial_number

parameters.description: The 6-digit code the MFA device shows now. Required with the device ARN.
parameters.name: mfa_token_code

parameters.description: Optional identity of the person behind the session, recorded in CloudTrail (2-64 characters).
parameters.name: source_identity

assumed_role_id.description: The role id and session name, 'AROA...:name'.

access_key_id.description: The temporary Access key ID (starts with ASIA).

expiration.description: When the credentials stop working (UTC ISO-8601).

secret_access_key.description: The temporary secret. Secret: whoever can read this workflow's run history can use it until it expires.

session_token.description: Send as X-Amz-Security-Token with the key and secret. Secret: whoever can read this workflow's run history can use it until it expires.

session_token_size.description: Size of the session token in bytes, when STS reports it.

session_token_utilization.description: Percentage of the maximum session token size used, when STS reports it.

decode_authorization_message.description: Decode the 'Encoded authorization failure message' from an AWS access-denied error, to see which policy denied what.
decode_authorization_message.name: decode_authorization_message

parameters.description: The encoded message from the error, or the whole error text. Line breaks are removed automatically.
parameters.name: encoded_message

decoded_message.description: The decoded authorization details (allowed, explicitDeny, matchedStatements, failures, context), or null if not valid JSON.

decoded_message_raw.description: The decoded message exactly as returned.

get_access_key_info.description: Find the AWS account that owns an access key ID, from any account. It does not say whether the key is still active.
get_access_key_info.display_str_template: Look up the account of access key {0}
get_access_key_info.name: get_access_key_info

parameters.description: The access key ID to look up, e.g. AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE.
parameters.name: access_key_id

account.description: The account that owns the key.

get_caller_identity.description: Show which AWS account and IAM principal the connection acts as. Needs no permissions, so it also tests the connection.
get_caller_identity.name: get_caller_identity

principal_name.description: Derived from the ARN: what follows the principal type.

principal_type.description: Derived from the ARN: user, assumed-role, federated-user or root.

user_id.description: The unique id of the calling user or role session.

get_federation_token.description: Issue temporary credentials for a named federated user, limited by a session policy you pass. The result contains a secret access key and session token: anyone who can see this workflow's run history can use them until they expire.
get_federation_token.name: get_federation_token

parameters.description: 2-32 letters, digits or _ + = , . @ -. It appears in the federated user's ARN.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: An IAM policy document (JSON) granting the session's permissions, intersected with the connected user's. Pass this or policy ARNs: without either the session has no permissions.
parameters.name: policy

parameters.description: Up to 10 managed policy ARNs (or AWS managed policy names such as 'ReadOnlyAccess') that further limit the session's permissions.
parameters.name: policy_arns

parameters.description: How long the result stays valid, 900-129600 seconds. Default 43200 (12 hours).
parameters.name: duration_seconds

parameters.description: Optional tags passed into the session as key/value pairs.
parameters.name: tags

access_key_id.description: The temporary Access key ID (starts with ASIA).

expiration.description: When the credentials stop working (UTC ISO-8601).

secret_access_key.description: The temporary secret. Secret: whoever can read this workflow's run history can use it until it expires.

session_token.description: Send as X-Amz-Security-Token with the key and secret. Secret: whoever can read this workflow's run history can use it until it expires.

session_token_size.description: Size of the session token in bytes, when STS reports it.

session_token_utilization.description: Percentage of the maximum session token size used, when STS reports it.

get_session_token.description: Issue temporary credentials with the connected user's own permissions, optionally MFA-authenticated. The result contains a secret access key and session token: anyone who can see this workflow's run history can use them until they expire.
get_session_token.name: get_session_token

parameters.description: How long the result stays valid, 900-129600 seconds. Default 43200 (12 hours).
parameters.name: duration_seconds

parameters.description: Only if MFA is required: the device's ARN (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:mfa/device-name), from IAM > Users > your user > Security credentials.
parameters.name: mfa_serial_number

parameters.description: The 6-digit code the MFA device shows now. Required with the device ARN.
parameters.name: mfa_token_code

access_key_id.description: The temporary Access key ID (starts with ASIA).

expiration.description: When the credentials stop working (UTC ISO-8601).

secret_access_key.description: The temporary secret. Secret: whoever can read this workflow's run history can use it until it expires.

session_token.description: Send as X-Amz-Security-Token with the key and secret. Secret: whoever can read this workflow's run history can use it until it expires.

session_token_size.description: Size of the session token in bytes, when STS reports it.

session_token_utilization.description: Percentage of the maximum session token size used, when STS reports it.

get_web_identity_token.description: Issue a signed JWT that proves this AWS identity to an external service (outbound identity federation). The token is a credential: anyone who can see this workflow's run history can present it until it expires.
get_web_identity_token.name: get_web_identity_token

parameters.description: 1-10 intended recipients, placed in the token's 'aud' claim, e.g. 'https://api.example.com'.
parameters.name: audience

parameters.description: How the token is signed.
parameters.name: signing_algorithm

parameters.description: How long the result stays valid, 60-3600 seconds. Default 300.
parameters.name: duration_seconds

parameters.description: Optional key/value pairs added to the token as claims.
parameters.name: tags

web_identity_token.description: A signed JWT identifying this AWS principal. Secret: whoever can read this workflow's run history can use it until it expires.

description: Use the AWS Security Token Service: check which account and identity a key belongs to, issue temporary credentials by assuming a role or requesting a session or federation token, decode access-denied messages, and issue JWTs for outbound federation.
